title: Oil Above $100: The Headwind Stocks Can't Shake
body:
Oil has once again become the stock market's biggest **headwind**. On Friday, U.S. crude (WTI) jumped 3.8% to $103.27 a barrel, while Brent, the global benchmark(기준 유종), settled at $116.72, its highest level since June 2022. Prices have climbed this far because the U.S. conflict with Iran has cut global supply, and traders seem **reluctant** to bet on a quick fix. Higher fuel prices raise **input costs** for airlines, factories and shippers, and those costs inevitably **eat into** profits. Consequently, nearly three in four S&P 500 stocks fell, and the index lost 0.5% to 7,623.68, its second weekly loss in a row. The Dow, which is packed with industrial and financial names, dropped even more, sliding 1.2%.

Bond markets offered little comfort. The 10-year Treasury yield edged up from 4.96% to 4.99%, as investors worried that **persistent** inflation would keep the Federal Reserve **hawkish**(매파적인, 긴축 선호); markets now lean toward another rate hike in December. Not every corner of the market suffered, though. Chipmakers such as Micron rose, which helped the Nasdaq limit its loss to 0.2%. In Seoul, the KOSPI had sunk as low as 5,305.98 during the session, but by the time the market closed, it had **clawed back** its losses to finish 0.3% higher at 5,550.30. Although that rebound is encouraging, it does not change the bigger picture: as long as oil stays above $100, stocks will struggle to find solid footing.
ko:
유가가 다시 한번 주식시장의 가장 큰 역풍이 됐다. 금요일 미국 원유(WTI)는 3.8% 뛰어 배럴당 103.27달러가 됐고, 국제 기준 유종인 브렌트유는 116.72달러로 마감해 2022년 6월 이후 최고치를 기록했다. 가격이 이렇게까지 오른 건 미국과 이란의 충돌로 세계 공급이 줄었기 때문인데, 트레이더들은 빠른 해결에 베팅하기를 꺼리는 모습이다. 연료값이 오르면 항공사·공장·해운사의 투입 비용이 커지고, 그 비용은 불가피하게 이익을 갉아먹는다. 그 결과 S&P 500 종목의 거의 4분의 3이 하락했고, 지수는 0.5% 내린 7,623.68로 2주 연속 주간 하락을 기록했다. 산업재·금융주 비중이 큰 다우지수는 1.2% 밀리며 더 크게 떨어졌다.

채권시장도 위안이 되지 못했다. 미 10년물 국채금리는 4.96%에서 4.99%로 소폭 올랐는데, 끈질긴 인플레이션 때문에 연준이 매파적 태도를 유지할 것이라는 걱정 때문이다. 시장은 이제 12월 추가 금리 인상 쪽으로 기울어 있다. 그래도 모든 곳이 다친 건 아니었다. 마이크론 같은 반도체주가 올라 나스닥은 하락 폭을 0.2%로 줄였다. 서울에서는 코스피가 장중 5,305.98까지 밀렸지만, 장이 끝날 무렵엔 손실을 되찾아 0.3% 오른 5,550.30으로 마감했다. 이 반등은 고무적이지만 큰 그림은 바뀌지 않는다. 유가가 100달러 위에 머무는 한 주식은 단단한 발판을 찾기 어려울 것이다.

vocab.en_easy: Something that slows down progress, like wind blowing against you when you run.
vocab.ex: High oil prices are a major headwind for airline stocks this quarter.

vocab.ko: (중앙은행이) 매파적인 — 물가 잡으려 금리 인상을 선호하는 (반대: dovish)
vocab.en_easy: Wanting to keep interest rates high to fight inflation.
vocab.ex: Stocks fell after the Fed chair sounded more hawkish than expected.

vocab.ko: 투입 비용(원자재·연료·인건비 등 생산에 드는 비용)
vocab.en_easy: The money a company spends on materials, energy, and other things it needs to make its products.
vocab.ex: Rising input costs forced the coffee shop near my gym to raise its prices.

vocab.en_easy: Not wanting to do something, so you hesitate before doing it.
vocab.ex: I was reluctant to go jogging in the rain, but I felt great afterward.

vocab.en_easy: Continuing for a long time and difficult to get rid of.
vocab.ex: Persistent inflation makes it hard for central banks to cut rates.

vocab.en_easy: To slowly use up or reduce something valuable.
vocab.ex: My long commute really eats into my workout time on weekdays.

vocab.en_easy: To slowly win back something you lost, with a lot of effort.
vocab.ex: The index clawed back most of its early losses by the afternoon.

grammar.point: 시간 표현 (by the time + 과거, 주절 had p.p.)
grammar.quote: by the time the market closed, it had clawed back its losses to finish 0.3% higher at 5,550.30.
grammar.explain_ko: by the time + 주어 + 과거동사 = '~할 무렵엔(이미)'. 그 시점보다 먼저 끝난 일은 주절에 과거완료(had p.p.)를 쓴다. 장 마감(과거) 시점에 '이미 만회를 끝냈다'는 순서가 had clawed back으로 드러난다. until(~까지 계속)과 달리 by the time은 '그때까지 완료'.
examples: By the time I got to the station, the last train had already left.
[OPIc] By the time we reached the top of the mountain, the sun had already set, so we just sat there and watched the city lights.

grammar.point: 현재완료 vs 과거 (has p.p. ↔ 과거 시점 부사)
grammar.quote: Prices have climbed this far because the U.S. conflict with Iran has cut global supply. … On Friday, U.S. crude (WTI) jumped 3.8%
grammar.explain_ko: 현재완료(have climbed)는 '지금까지 쌓인 결과'를 말할 때, 과거(jumped)는 On Friday·yesterday·in 2022 같은 '끝난 특정 시점'과 함께 쓴다. 'On Friday, crude has jumped'처럼 명확한 과거 시점 부사와 현재완료를 같이 쓰면 틀린다(수능 어법 단골).
examples: The Fed has raised rates twice this year, and it raised them again last month.
[OPIc] I've been to Gyeongju three times, but the trip I took last spring was definitely the best.

tense.sentence: Oil has once again become the stock market's biggest headwind.
tense.why_ko: 과거부터 이어진 흐름이 '지금' 결과(가장 큰 악재인 상태)로 남아 있어서 현재완료.

tense.sentence: the KOSPI had sunk as low as 5,305.98 during the session
tense.why_ko: 장 마감(과거)보다 '더 먼저' 일어난 장중 급락이라 had p.p. — 두 과거 사건의 순서를 보여 준다.

review.q: Worries about another rate hike continued to ______ bank stocks, which fell for the third straight day.
review.exp_ko: weigh on = ~에 부담을 주다(주가를 누르다). 'fell for the third straight day'(3일 연속 하락)가 단서. draw on(~을 활용하다)·count on(~에 의지하다)은 긍정·중립 의미, dwell on(곰곰이 생각하다)은 사람 주어가 필요해 '걱정이 주가를 누른다'는 뜻이 안 된다.

review.q: The Fed chair said nothing to ______ another hike in December, so traders kept betting on higher rates.
review.exp_ko: rule out = (가능성을) 배제하다. '아무 말도 안 해서 → 인상 베팅 유지' = 인상 가능성을 배제하지 않았다. leave out(빠뜨리다)은 목록에서 빼는 것, point out(지적하다)·figure out(알아내다)은 '가능성 배제' 의미가 없다.

review.q: Because jet fuel prices jumped again, the airline added a fuel ______ of about $40 to every international ticket.
review.exp_ko: fuel surcharge = 유류할증료(기본요금 위에 붙는 추가 요금)로 굳은 연어. fare는 '운임 그 자체'라 '추가'하는 대상이 아니고, toll은 도로·다리 통행료, premium은 보험료·웃돈이라 '연료비 때문에 덧붙는 요금'과 연어가 맞지 않는다.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"In Seoul, the KOSPI had sunk as low as 5,305.98 during the session, but by the time the market closed, it had ______ its losses to finish 0.3% higher."
quiz.exp_ko: 장중 급락 후 '손실을 만회해' 상승 마감 = clawed back (its losses). held back(억제하다)은 '손실을 억눌렀다'가 되어 상승 마감과 연결이 약하고, paid back(빚을 갚다)은 losses와 연어가 아니며, cut back(줄이다·삭감하다)은 cut back on 지출처럼 쓰여 '되찾다' 의미가 없다.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"Oil (A)has once again become the market's biggest headwind. On Friday, Brent (B)settled at $116.72. Since early October, prices (C)have climbed sharply, and on the same day the 10-year yield (D)has edged up to 4.99%."
quiz.exp_ko: (D) 'on the same day'(그날 = 금요일)는 끝난 특정 과거 시점 → 과거형 edged up 이어야 한다. (A)는 지금까지의 결과라 현재완료 OK, (B)는 On Friday와 과거형 OK, (C)는 Since early October(~이후 지금까지)와 현재완료 OK.

quiz.q: [요지] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Expensive oil, by raising costs and keeping rates high, is the main force holding stocks back.
Chipmakers have replaced energy firms as the main drivers of the U.S. stock market today.
The KOSPI's late rebound shows that Asian markets have stopped reacting to oil prices.
Rising bond yields, rather than oil, explain most of Friday's broad decline in U.S. stocks.
quiz.exp_ko: 첫 문장(유가 = 가장 큰 역풍)과 마지막 문장(유가 100달러 위면 주식 고전)이 주제문 → ①. ②반도체 상승은 '예외'(Not every corner)로만 등장, ③코스피 반등은 '큰 그림은 안 바뀐다'고 했고, ④금리는 유가→인플레이션→연준으로 이어진 '부수 결과'라 원인 순서가 뒤집혔다.

quiz.q: [내용 일치·추론] 본문의 숫자로 판단할 때 옳은 것은?
choices: In percentage terms, the Dow's drop was less than five times the Nasdaq's.
The price gap between Brent and WTI was less than $10 a barrel.
From its intraday low, the KOSPI rose by roughly 4.6% to its close.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose by about 3 percentage points on Friday.

talk.topic: Oil over $100 — 기름값이 오르면 내 지갑과 주식은?
talk.setting_ko: 월요일 아침 회사 탕비실. 주말에 주유하고 온 동료 B와 주식 하는 A가 유가 얘기를 한다.

dialogue.en: I filled up my car on Saturday and almost had a heart attack. Gas is crazy right now.
dialogue.ko: 토요일에 기름 넣다가 심장 멎는 줄 알았어. 요즘 기름값 미쳤어.

dialogue.en: Yeah, everyone's feeling the pinch. Brent closed above $116 on Friday — highest since 2022.
dialogue.ko: 응, 다들 쪼들려. 브렌트유가 금요일에 116달러 넘게 마감했대 — 2022년 이후 최고야.

dialogue.en: Is that why the market's been so weak?
Pretty much. When fuel gets expensive, companies either eat the cost or pass it on to customers. Either way, someone gets hurt.
dialogue.ko: 거의 그렇지. 연료가 비싸지면 회사가 비용을 떠안거나 소비자한테 넘기거든. 어느 쪽이든 누군가는 다쳐.

dialogue.en: And there's no end in sight with the whole Iran situation, right?
dialogue.ko: 이란 상황도 끝이 안 보이잖아, 그치?

dialogue.en: Not really. Plus, rates might go up again in December, so I'm bracing for a bumpy few weeks.
dialogue.ko: 별로. 게다가 12월에 금리가 또 오를 수도 있어서, 몇 주 출렁일 거라고 각오하고 있어.

dialogue.en: Maybe I should just start biking to work.
Honestly? Not a bad idea — free cardio, too.
dialogue.ko: 진짜로? 나쁘지 않은데 — 공짜 유산소도 되고.

expressions.ex: With rent and gas going up, a lot of young people are feeling the pinch.

expressions.when_ko: 주유 얘기할 때 — OPIc 국내여행 '출발 준비' 묘사에 바로 씀
expressions.ex: We filled up the car and grabbed some snacks before hitting the highway.

expressions.when_ko: 회사가 원가 상승분을 가격에 반영할 때
expressions.ex: The café passed the higher milk prices on to customers.
The construction near my place started in spring, and there's no end in sight.

expressions.when_ko: 안 좋은 일이 올 걸 예상하고 각오할 때
expressions.ex: Traders are bracing for more volatility ahead of the Fed meeting.

your_turn.q_en: How do rising prices, like gas or food, affect your daily life these days?
your_turn.hint_ko: ①체감한 순간(주유·장보기) ②바꾼 습관 1~2개 ③느낀 점 — feel the pinch, pass on to 써 보기
your_turn.sample_answer: Honestly, I've been feeling the pinch lately. Last weekend I filled up my car and it cost way more than it did a few months ago. Even my favorite café has passed the higher costs on to customers — my latte went up by almost five hundred won. So I've made a couple of changes: I take the subway more often, and I make coffee at home on weekdays. It's a little annoying, but I'm kind of saving money and getting more steps in, so it's not all bad.

talk.topic: 집에서 보내는 휴가 — 연휴 계획 짜기 (Background Survey #55)
talk.setting_ko: 다음 주 연차를 앞두고 친구 B가 어디 가냐고 묻자, A는 '집콕 휴가'를 계획 중이라고 말한다.

dialogue.en: So, any big plans for your days off next week?
dialogue.ko: 그래서 다음 주 쉬는 날에 큰 계획 있어?

dialogue.en: Not really. I'm thinking of just staying home and recharging my batteries.
A staycation, huh? Doesn't that get boring?
Not at all. Day one, I'm sleeping in. Then I'll order in some chicken and binge-watch a whole series.
dialogue.ko: 전혀. 첫날은 늦잠 잘 거야. 그다음엔 치킨 시켜 먹으면서 시리즈 하나 몰아볼 거고.

dialogue.en: That actually sounds amazing. What about the gym?
I'll still do a light workout in the mornings, but nothing crazy.
dialogue.ko: 아침에 가볍게는 하겠지만 빡세게는 안 해.

dialogue.en: If you get bored, I'm up for a walk by the river one evening.
dialogue.ko: 심심하면 저녁에 한강 산책 한 번 콜이야.

expressions.when_ko: 쉬면서 에너지를 채운다고 말할 때 — OPIc 집 휴가·여행 단골
expressions.ex: I spend my vacations at home because I really need to recharge my batteries.

expressions.when_ko: 쉬는 날 일부러 늦게 일어날 때 (oversleep = 실수로 늦잠)
expressions.ex: On the first day of my vacation, I always sleep in until noon.

expressions.when_ko: 요리 대신 배달 음식 먹을 때
expressions.ex: We were too tired to cook, so we just ordered in some pizza.

expressions.when_ko: 한 번에 여러 화를 연달아 볼 때
expressions.ex: I binge-watched an entire season in one weekend.
I'm up for a coffee after the workout if you are.

your_turn.q_en: What do you usually do when you have a vacation at home?
your_turn.hint_ko: ①집 휴가를 좋아하는 이유 ②1일차→2일차 순서 ③꼭 하는 것(운동·산책) — recharge, sleep in, order in 넣기
your_turn.sample_answer: Well, when I have a few days off, I usually just stay home and recharge my batteries. On the first day, I sleep in — like, really late — and then I order in something greasy, usually fried chicken. After that, I binge-watch a series I've been saving. But I don't just lie around the whole time. I still go to the gym in the morning, and in the evening I take a long walk by the river. It's simple, but by the end of it I feel totally refreshed.

opic.survey_topic: 국내 여행 (Background Survey #56) · 월요일 콤보: 묘사 → 루틴 → 과거 경험

combo.q_en: You indicated in the survey that you enjoy traveling within your country. Tell me about one of your favorite places to visit in Korea. Where is it, and what does it look like? Please describe it in as much detail as possible.
combo.q_ko: 서베이에서 국내 여행을 즐긴다고 하셨는데요. 한국에서 가장 좋아하는 여행지 하나를 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고 어떻게 생겼나요? 최대한 자세히 묘사해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(장소 + 한 줄 인상) → 본문 ① 위치·가는 법 ② 눈에 보이는 것(바다·골목·건물 — 오감 디테일) ③ 분위기·좋아하는 이유 → 마무리(추천 한 줄). 묘사는 현재시제 중심, There is/are·You can see ~ 반복 대신 'What stands out is ~', 'It's surrounded by ~'로 변주. IH/AL: 공간을 '멀리→가까이' 순서로 그리는 문단 구성, 색·소리·냄새 디테일, 필러 1~2회.
combo.model_answer: Okay, one of my favorite places in Korea has to be Gangneung, on the east coast. It's about two hours from Seoul by KTX, so it's perfect for a quick getaway. Well, when you get there, the first thing you notice is the ocean — it's this deep, clear blue, and the beach is really wide, with soft, almost white sand. Along the coast, there's a long street packed with cafés, and that's actually what Gangneung is famous for. You know, you can sit on a rooftop, drink a hand-drip coffee, and just watch the waves. What stands out to me, though, is the pine forest right behind the beach. It smells amazing, and it's really quiet, so it's great for a morning walk or even a light jog. In the evening, the whole area lights up, and you can hear people laughing by the water. I mean, it's not fancy or anything, but it feels relaxing in a way Seoul never does. So if you ever visit Korea, I'd definitely recommend Gangneung.

key_phrases.en: What stands out to me is ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '바다 있어요, 카페 있어요' 나열, IH는 바다→거리→숲처럼 공간 순서로 묶기, AL은 '서울과 대비'처럼 비교 문장으로 의미를 정리하며 끝낸다.

combo.q_en: What do you usually do to prepare for a trip? Tell me about the things you typically do before you leave, step by step.
combo.q_ko: 여행 준비를 위해 보통 무엇을 하나요? 떠나기 전에 주로 하는 일을 단계별로 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(준비 스타일 한 줄: 꼼꼼형/즉흥형) → 본문 ① 1~2주 전(숙소·교통 예약) ② 며칠 전(맛집·코스 검색, 날씨) ③ 전날·당일(짐 싸기, 주유·간식) → 마무리(준비가 여행에 주는 의미). 현재시제 + 빈도부사(usually, always, tend to), 순서 연결어(a week or two before, once ~, the night before, by the time). 오늘 시사 표현 fill up 재활용.
combo.model_answer: Well, I'd say I'm kind of a planner, so I usually start getting ready about two weeks before a trip. First, I book a place to stay — I tend to look for a small guesthouse with good reviews rather than a big hotel. Then I check the train schedule, or if I'm driving, I just make sure the car is ready. A few days before I leave, I look up local restaurants and make a rough plan, like, one or two must-see spots a day, not too much. I also check the weather, because, you know, one rainy day can totally change the plan. The night before, I pack — honestly, I always pack running shoes, because I like jogging in a new place early in the morning. And on the day I leave, I fill up the car, grab some snacks and a coffee, and make a playlist for the road. By the time I'm on the highway, I already feel like I'm on vacation. So yeah, for me, preparing is actually half the fun.
combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '예약하고 짐 싸요'로 끝, IH는 '2주 전→며칠 전→전날→당일' 시간 순서, AL은 이유(왜 게스트하우스·왜 운동화)를 붙여 습관에 성격을 입힌다.

combo.q_en: Tell me about a memorable trip you took in Korea. When was it, who did you go with, and what happened that made it so special?
combo.q_ko: 한국에서 다녀온 기억에 남는 여행에 대해 말해 주세요. 언제였고, 누구와 갔으며, 무슨 일이 있어서 특별했나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·어디·누구, 한 줄 요약) → 본문 ① 배경(계획) ② 사건(예상 밖의 일 — 문제나 반전) ③ 해결·감정 → 마무리(지금 돌아보면 / 배운 점). 과거시제 일관 + 그보다 앞선 일은 had p.p.(오늘 문법 by the time). IH/AL: 사건에 긴장감(But then, all of a sudden), 대사 한 줄 인용, 감정 단어, 마지막에 현재와 연결.
combo.model_answer: Let me think… I'd have to say the trip I took to Jeju with two of my college friends, about three years ago. We'd planned it for months, and our main goal was to hike Hallasan, the highest mountain in Korea. So on the second day, we got up at like four a.m. and started climbing. But then, about halfway up, the weather suddenly changed — it got foggy and really windy, and one of my friends started to feel dizzy. Honestly, we were kind of scared. We had a quick talk and decided to turn back, which was really disappointing at the time. But here's the thing: on the way down, the fog cleared up, and we ended up at a tiny noodle place at the bottom of the mountain. We were so hungry that it was, like, the best meal of my life. By the time we got back to our guesthouse, we were laughing about the whole thing. Looking back, I think that trip taught me that plans don't always work out, and that's totally okay. We still talk about that noodle place whenever we meet.
combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '제주 갔고 재밌었어요', IH는 배경→사건→해결 3단 구성, AL은 had p.p.로 시간 순서를 정확히 하고 '배운 점·지금과의 연결'로 이야기를 닫는다.

opic.practice_ko: 묘사(강릉 대신 본인 여행지로 바꿔서) 1개를 타이머 90초로 녹음 → 다시 들으며 '현재시제 유지'와 'What stands out ~' 사용 여부 체크. 과거 경험은 had p.p.를 최소 1번 넣어 2분 녹음.

최근 7일 증권사 리포트 중 화장품·소비재 테마는 29건이고 이 중 '낙관' 톤이 14건, 바이오·헬스케어 테마는 22건이고 이 중 '낙관'이 10건이었다. 테마 내 '낙관' 비중은 화장품·소비재가 바이오·헬스케어보다 몇 %p 높은가?
